radiology_report:
Subject: Prostate Multiparametric MRI | Date: 20 February 2025 | Site: Amsterdam UMC, AMC

Indication: Reassessment after a previous positive biopsy result. Current serum PSA reads 6.9 ng/mL.

Imaging reveals a glandular volume of 26.9 mL. A distinct hypointense area occupies the right peripheral zone, spanning from the mid-gland down to the apex, with dimensions of roughly 14 by 11 by 10 mm. Diffusion-weighted and ADC sequences highlight pronounced restriction. Dynamic contrast phases show rapid, robust enhancement. Capsular borders remain intact without seminal vesicle infiltration. Pelvic nodal basins appear normal. Skeletal survey shows no malignant deposits.

Conclusion: PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone. Prostate volume 26.9 mL yielding a PSA density of 0.257 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.84531116.

previous_notes.author: Dr. M. Jansen (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinic assessment conducted after the first positive prostate biopsy. March 2024 laboratory results recorded a PSA value of 5.6 ng/mL, which triggered a urology consultation for diagnostic workup and magnetic resonance imaging coordination. Conservative observation continued during the waiting period, encompassing standard blood panels and symptom checks. Subsequent tracking captured an increase to 6.9 ng/mL alongside awaiting imaging outcomes, completing the primary care documentation cycle.
